extracted_claims.text: Under Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, high-risk AI systems have two conformity-assessment routes: internal control under Annex VI (provider self-assessment of QMS), or third-party assessment involving a notified body under Annex VII (assessment of quality management system and technical documentation).

Annex VII (notified body) assessment is required for high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification) where harmonised standards or common specifications have not been applied, or where the provider has not applied them fully; otherwise internal control (Annex VI) or a notified body route may be chosen.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., machinery, medical devices), the provider must follow the conformity assessment procedure required by that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements of the AI Act.

Providers may choose any notified body for the Annex VII conformity assessment procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or EU institutions/bodies/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

If a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, a new conformity assessment is required, except where changes to continuously learning systems were predetermined by the provider and assessed as part of the initial conformity assessment.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to derogate from the standard conformity assessment procedure (Article 43) and authorise placing a specific high-risk AI system on the market for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Article 44 covers certificates issued by notified bodies, Article 45 covers information obligations of notified bodies, Article 47 covers the EU declaration of conformity, and Article 48 covers CE marking, as part of the Section 5 framework on standards, conformity assessment, certificates and registration.

Annex VII, point 4.5, grants notified bodies access to training and trained models of an AI system, including relevant parameters, if necessary to assess conformity with Chapter III Section 2 requirements, after other reasonable verification means have been exhausted, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative requirements for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

The Council document ST-7322-2026 references categories/codes for AI systems subject to Annex I.A, tied to the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 of the Regulation (implementing act context).

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 COD) would create a new Annex XIV listing categories/types of AI systems for the NANDO notified-body information system, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, but this is a proposal, not adopted law as of the source date.
As of March 2026, no AI Act notified bodies had yet completed designation; the designation ecosystem across member states was still being built, with limited capacity and uncertain timelines.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device AI systems.

A 2026 industry guide states that 'Post-2026' notified bodies designated under the AI Act will begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, implying none existed as of that writing in 2026.
As of October 2025, NANDO lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, under the Medical Devices Regulation framework (not AI-Act-specific designations).

A 2026-09-15 legal analysis states the obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems were moved from 2 December 2027 to 2 August 2029 under a 'final text agreed in September 2026', citing lack of readiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies.

A 2026-09-22 legal analysis similarly states that Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from 2 August 2029, replacing the 2 December 2027 date set by the 'AI Omnibus', and that until then providers do not need a conformity assessment by a notified body for Annex III systems.

A 2026-09-29 client alert confirms the EU institutions deferred application of AI Act high-risk requirements for Annex III systems to 2 August 2029, to give time for harmonised standards and first notified bodies to be designated.

Other sources (industry/news blogs, undated) state that high-risk AI obligations, including conformity assessment, 'fully apply' from August 2026, or that a 'August 2026 deadline isn't moving', which conflicts with the later 2026 legal-analysis sources reporting deferral to 2 August 2029.

The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), a separate EU regulation (not the AI Act), had its notified-body rules start applying 11 June 2026, with zero CRA notified bodies designated as of late June 2026 and a target of sufficient notified body capacity by 11 December 2026; full CRA application is 11 December 2027.
Article 43(5) of the AI Act gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to update Annex VI and Annex VII procedures in light of technical progress.

open_issues: No source confirms that any notified body has actually been formally designated under the AI Act as of the most recent sources (dated through September 2026); several sources explicitly state that none had been designated as of March/April 2026, and no later source reports a change.

It remains unclear whether the 'AI Omnibus' and the September 2026 'final text' changing the Annex III deadline to 2 August 2029 have been formally adopted as amendments to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, or whether they are still proposals—none of the sources provide a citation to an official consolidated legal text confirming adoption.

The relationship between the proposed new Annex XIV / NANDO integration (COM(2025) 836) and the existing NANDO notified body codes referenced in the Council document (ST-7322-2026) is unclear, including whether the proposal has been adopted.

No source provides a definitive, current list of specific notified bodies designated under the AI Act (as opposed to under MDR/IVDR or CRA), leaving open exactly which organizations, if any, hold AI Act notified body status as of October 2026.

The precise timeline and criteria the Commission and Member States will use to ramp up notified body capacity for AI Act conformity assessments (akin to the CRA's 11 December 2026 capacity target) is not addressed by any source for the AI Act specifically.

It is unclear from the sources exactly which systems under Annex III require mandatory third-party (Annex VII) assessment versus internal control (Annex VI), beyond biometric identification/critical infrastructure examples cited inconsistently across industry blogs.

Whether the August 2026 dates cited by some undated/industry sources refer to GPAI model obligations, Annex I product-integrated high-risk systems, or Annex III high-risk systems specifically is not clearly disambiguated across sources, creating ambiguity about which obligations are truly affected by the 2029 deferral.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act, and the State of Notified Body Designations

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control (Annex VI) and third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on the system's category and whether harmonised standards have been applied (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). However, as of the most recent sources (through September 2026), no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated under the AI Act itself, and there is significant disagreement across sources about whether high-risk compliance deadlines remain set for August 2026 or have been deferred to August 2029 (low-to-medium confidence, contested).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 establishes that high-risk AI systems may undergo either internal control under Annex VI (provider self-assessment of its quality management system) or third-party assessment involving a notified body under Annex VII, which examines the quality management system and technical documentation (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Notified body (Annex VII) assessment is specifically required for biometric identification systems under Annex III point 1 where harmonised standards or common specifications have not been fully applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For high-risk AI systems embedded in products already covered by sectoral EU legislation (e.g., machinery, medical devices under Annex I Section A), providers must follow that sector's existing conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU bodies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the notified body role (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications to a high-risk system trigger a new conformity assessment, unless changes to continuously learning systems were predetermined and already assessed (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard procedures and authorise limited-period market placement for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Related provisions include Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), and Article 48 (CE marking) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)). Annex VII also grants notified bodies access to training and trained models, including parameters, when necessary for conformity assessment, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Multiple sources indicate that, as of March–April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act, with designation infrastructure still under development across member states (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AI Act Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [MDXCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)). By contrast, NANDO lists 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies as of October 2025, though these are under the Medical Devices Regulation framework, not AI Act-specific designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). # Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act, and the State of Notified Body Designations

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control (Annex VI) and third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on the system's category and whether harmonised standards have been applied (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). However, as of the most recent sources (through September 2026), no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated under the AI Act itself, and there is significant disagreement across sources about whether high-risk compliance deadlines remain set for August 2026 or have been deferred to August 2029 (low-to-medium confidence, contested).

## Key Findings

Article 43 establishes that high-risk AI systems may undergo either internal control under Annex VI (provider self-assessment of its quality management system) or third-party assessment involving a notified body under Annex VII, which examines the quality management system and technical documentation (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Notified body (Annex VII) assessment is specifically required for biometric identification systems under Annex III point 1 where harmonised standards or common specifications have not been fully applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For high-risk AI systems embedded in products already covered by sectoral EU legislation (e.g., machinery, medical devices under Annex I Section A), providers must follow that sector's existing conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU bodies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the notified body role (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications to a high-risk system trigger a new conformity assessment, unless changes to continuously learning systems were predetermined and already assessed (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). ### Timeline Disputes
